citation.authors: Ramesh D, Haney M, Cooper ZD
citation.title: Marijuana's dose-dependent effects in daily marijuana smokers
citation.retrieval_method: full HTML text fetched directly from PMC article viewer (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), verified as complete article (abstract through references, all 5 figure captions and both tables present)

ramesh-2013.setting: New York State Psychiatric Institute, outpatient laboratory; part of a larger 8-session naltrexone/marijuana interaction study (only placebo-naltrexone sessions reported here)
ramesh-2013.analysis_note: 19 participants completed the study; data from 1 volunteer excluded due to experimental error, leaving N=18 for analysis
ramesh-2013.population: non-treatment-seeking daily marijuana smokers, 21-45 years old
ramesh-2013.inclusion_criteria: smoking >=3 marijuana cigarettes 4x/week for the prior month; healthy per physical exam/ECG/blood chemistry; marijuana use confirmed by urine toxicology and self-report; no repeated use of other drugs (except nicotine/alcohol/caffeine); no current DSM-IV-TR Axis I psychopathology; females excluded if pregnant/nursing/not using contraception

demographics.other_notes: 7 participants reported daily cigarette smoking (4.9 +/- 0.9 cigarettes/day); 10 reported drinking alcohol weekly (2.0 +/- 0.2 days/week, 2.7 +/- 0.4 drinks/occasion)

ramesh-2013.condition_detail: Every session, participants smoked 6 total puffs from 3 marijuana cigarettes (2 puffs/cigarette, 5-s inhale, 10-s hold, 40-s interpuff interval). The number of ACTIVE vs inactive cigarettes varied by condition: 0 puffs = 3 inactive cigarettes; 2 puffs = 1 active + 2 inactive; 4 puffs = 2 active + 1 inactive; 6 puffs = 3 active. Active puffs were always smoked before inactive puffs within a session. Randomized within-subject design; all participants exposed to all 4 conditions.

product.note: Due to limited supply of the 6.2% THC stock, the first 13 participants smoked 6.2% THC active cigarettes and the final 5 smoked 5.5% THC; strength was held consistent within each participant across their sessions.

outcome_domains: expired carbon monoxide (CO, Bedfont Micro Smokerlyzer)
MRF: strength, good effect, bad effect, liking, take-again (5-item VAS)
SE-VAS: 44-item mood/physical-symptom VAS incl. 'high', 'stimulated', 'I want marijuana'
task battery: repeated acquisition, divided attention (DAT), digit-symbol substitution (DSST), digit recall (DRT)
amount of marijuana smoked (pre/post cigarette weight difference)
ramesh-2013.statistics_method: Repeated-measures ANOVA with planned comparisons, Huynh-Feldt corrected; significance threshold p<=.05; six planned pairwise comparisons per dependent variable (0v2, 0v4, 0v6, 2v4, 2v6, 4v6 active puffs)

citation.authors: Bidwell LC, YorkWilliams SL, Mueller RL, Bryan AD, Hutchison KE
citation.title: Association of naturalistic administration of cannabis flower and concentrates with intoxication and impairment
citation.retrieval_method: full HTML text fetched directly from PMC article viewer, verified complete (Key Points/Abstract through Conclusions, Table 1, Table 2, all 3 figures, Discussion, Limitations present)

bidwell-2020.design_detail: Cohort study, between-groups design, with random assignment to higher- vs lower-THC product WITHIN user group (flower users randomized to 16% or 24% THC; concentrate users randomized to 70% or 90% THC). No random assignment to flower-vs-concentrate group itself (ethically precluded) and no placebo condition (does not exist in the legal market). Registered as observational study, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03522103.
bidwell-2020.setting: Mobile laboratory, community/university setting (University of Colorado Boulder); ad libitum use occurred at participants' own residence, purchased from a single Colorado dispensary (The Farm)
bidwell-2020.analysis_note: 133 individuals enrolled and assessed. 12 participants excluded from analysis due to very low postuse THC (<0.02 ug/mL vs study mean 0.24 [SD 0.35] ug/mL), indicating non-compliance with the ad libitum use protocol. Final analyzed N=121: 55 flower users, 66 concentrate users.
bidwell-2020.population: regular cannabis users, self-selected as flower-preferring or concentrate-preferring, ages 21-70
bidwell-2020.inclusion_criteria: used cannabis >=4 times in past month; prior use of the highest potency assignable in the study (24% THC flower or 90% THC concentrate) without adverse reaction; no other non-prescription drug use in past 60 days (urine-confirmed); no daily tobacco use; alcohol use <=2x/week and <=3 drinks/occasion; not pregnant/trying to conceive; not in treatment for psychotic or bipolar disorder

demographics.note: Concentrate group reported more frequent current concentrate use and had greater blood THC/metabolites at baseline (pre-use), reflecting greater long-term THC exposure. Table 1 (not yet fully extracted here) additionally breaks demographics/baseline cannabinoid levels down by potency subgroup (16%/24% flower, 70%/90% concentrate).

bidwell-2020.condition_detail: Flower users randomly assigned to purchase 3g of 16% or 24% THC flower; concentrate users randomly assigned to purchase 1g of 70% or 90% THC concentrate, from a single state-licensed dispensary with ISO 17025-accredited lab-tested potency labeling. 5-day ad libitum familiarization period, then a mobile-laboratory experimental day: preuse assessment, then ad libitum use at home via participant's preferred administration method (mean 13.3 min away, SD 7, range 3-47 min), then short-term-postuse assessment, then 1-hour-postuse assessment.
outcome_domains: subjective drug effects: ARCI-marijuana scale, POMS tension, POMS vigor, self-reported intoxication (avg of feeling high/mentally stoned/physically stoned)
cognition: inhibitory control (flanker), episodic memory (picture task), working memory, delayed verbal recall errors (shopping list)
balance: postural sway, eyes open / eyes closed / eyes closed+head back
bidwell-2020.statistics_method: Mixed-effect models / repeated-measures ANOVA testing linear and quadratic time effects, main effect of cannabis form (flower vs concentrate), and form-by-time interactions; each model covaried for the measure's own baseline value.
data_ambiguity_flags: Abstract text states plasma THC 'were 0.32 (SE = 0.43) ug/mL in concentrate users ... and 0.14 (SE = 0.16) ug/mL in flower users.' The Discussion section restates the identical numbers as 'mean [SD] of 0.32 [0.43]' and 'mean [SD] of 0.14 [0.16]' -- i.e. the same variability figures are labeled SE in the Abstract and SD in the Discussion. Table 2's model-based SEs for short-term THC are much smaller (flower 0.03, concentrate 0.02), consistent with the Discussion's SD labeling being the more plausible reading (population SD, not a model SE) but this project does not resolve the discrepancy -- both labels are preserved verbatim in content/claims.json rather than silently picked.
